findings.title: Reuse an SLA detail fragment within each operation
findings.failure: The same six-status selection is duplicated 12 times. Future status or timestamp changes require coordinated edits across every target, allowing their response shapes to drift.
findings.fix: Define one operation-prefixed fragment on ServiceLevelAgreementStatusDetail in each file and spread it into the four targets. Keep fragment names unique across files.
findings.evidence: A read-only comparison confirmed all 12 selections are identical. services/mcp-server/operations/updateBroadcast.graphql:120–173 already uses named fragments to reuse repeated selections. tools/graphql-lint/validateMcpOperations.ts combines all operation definitions, so fragment names must remain globally unique.

checked_fine: Deploy: Dockerfile copies the operations directory, mcp.config.yaml loads it, and McpServerStack packages that directory with ContainerImage.fromAsset. All required schema fields already exist at HEAD~1; no new deployment ordering, environment, secret, permission, resource ownership, or export dependency was introduced.

Contract: Programmatic comparison against HEAD~1 confirmed all previous selections, arguments, variable defaults, sorting and pagination remain unchanged in all three operations. New SLA variables are nullable and default to null.
Contract: All six selected SLA variants and their timestamps match schema.ts and resolvers.ts. Transport routes, headers, authentication and network policy are unchanged.
Data: These changes only extend queries; no writes, migrations, deletion policies or retention changes.

Silent regression: threadsFilter.ts defaults omitted updatedAt to null; threadDbFilterUtils.ts:943 explicitly treats the resulting all-null SLA filter as a no-op. Existing unfiltered calls retain their results.

Silent regression: The summary uses the existing batched tracker loader without an additional permission requirement. Threads with neither a tier nor an SLA policy return four null targets without loading trackers. Historical filter matching is explicitly documented.
Operability: Operation files remain part of the deployed container asset; existing logging, health checks and scaling configuration are unchanged.
Rollback: HEAD~1 already supports the queried schema and resolver behavior. Rolling back removes the new MCP fields and filters but requires no data repair or infrastructure reversal.
Blast radius: Only three MCP operation files changed; shared schemas, helpers, constants and other consumers are unchanged.

Dead code: Repository-wide git grep for operation-directory consumers and new variable names, plus selection tracing, found all additions reachable through the configured operation loader; both new variables are consumed.

Validation scope: Static review and read-only parity checks completed. GraphQL validation and local integration tests were not run because node_modules is absent; no dependencies were installed and no network was used.
